biggest_leak: The claim-page email gate is the biggest and most review-critical leak, so I am attacking it -- but this cycle by REPAIRING the diagnostic instrument that will tell us WHY people leave, rather than piling a blind conversion change onto ground that is spent for presentation (PR #8) and closed to the code-first move (owner-rejected), and rather than betting on an unverified cause the way the last cycle did.

choice_reasoning.expected_value_to_reviews: Indirect but the highest available. The claim gate produces every video and thus (via the in-app thank-you) essentially every review. choice_reasoning.already_tried_here: Coverage map: claim landed->email has 1 real conversion attempt (PR #8 layout/hierarchy rebuild -> flat 44.5%->39.0%), one owner-rejected proposal (code-first), and one measurement-only ship (2026-07-20 instrumentation). Presentation reshuffles are explicitly spent; code-first is explicitly rejected. What is NOT spent is making the leak diagnosable -- 2026-07-20 started that and this change finishes it correctly.
choice_reasoning.what_history_suggests: Pattern across all changes: the one durable WIN (2026-06-16) changed a MECHANISM (email-first delivery) on a warm-user step; the one FLAT attempt (PR #8) was a claim-page presentation reshuffle; the message-step copy tweak is unprovable at this traffic. So mechanism changes on the right step move this funnel, presentation reshuffles do not -- and nothing moves without a correct measurement to read it. That argues: fix measurement here first, then make a mechanism (not presentation) bet next cycle once the cause is visible.
choice_reasoning.why_not_the_others: Leak 2 (email->video) is high value but its losing sub-step cannot be localised this cycle (PostHog 403, no Supabase in-app 'arrived' event) -- a fix would bet on an unverified cause. Leak 3 (preview/share review ask) is the biggest percentage but the lowest EV: a redundant second ask after the in-app thank-you already harvests review intent, already attacked once with no effect, and the adjacent email surface was just owner-rejected.

findings_addressed: Minor #1 (third consecutive measurement-only cycle; owner names conversion as the target): Acknowledged and carried into this report and the changelog. The repair is genuinely time-boxed -- it must land before the ~2026-08-03/05 read accumulates or a month of accumulation is lost -- and every conversion alternative this cycle would bet on a cause that cannot be verified (PostHog query api 403, no in-app replays), the exact mistake the last cycle was faulted for. Per the plan's own commitment, the NEXT cycle must produce a mechanism-level conversion bet driven by the repaired read; the never-attacked in-app examples/occasion (role -> pressed Create) screen is the leading candidate. A fourth measurement-only cycle would not be defensible.

Minor #2 (a documented [FACT] in FUNNEL_CONTEXT is now wrong -- claim traffic arrives with code=GOTYOU30 & source=insert|box, not '?sku only'): Raised to the owner as a FACT-correction and strategic question in tradeoff.unverified_assumptions, NOT used as a lever, and I built nothing on it. Showing a code up front remains owner-rejected. Owner should confirm whether GOTYOU30 is a real multi-use printed code (if so it weakens the 'discount is the price of the email' premise) and resolve the FUNNEL_CONTEXT [FACT]. Not acted on this cycle.

Minor #3 (fix rests on 'input' firing on autofill/paste; spec-correct but browser-dependent, cannot be sized from N=6): Addressed in verification -- I drove the actual edited code and exercised (a) an input-only path with no focus (autofill/paste), confirming exactly ONE email_field_engaged via the shared once-flag, and (b) a storage-blocked session, confirming all three claim events share one module-scoped in-memory visitor_id. Adding 'input' strictly improves coverage over focus-only with no downside; residual risk is only prevalence, which is flagged.

change.title: Fix the behind-the-scenes counter on the claim page so it correctly counts everyone who touches the email box
change.targets: Claim page: landed -> gave email (its diagnostic instrumentation -- email_field_engaged and visitor_id linking added 2026-07-20). No conversion event touched.
change.expected_effect: No conversion effect (and none claimed). Effect is measurement fidelity: email_field_engaged becomes a true count of everyone who touches the email box (including autofill/paste), and visitors in private/in-app browsers stay linkable, so the 'did they touch the box at all vs touched it and didn't submit' split is computable and correct at the read due in early August.
change.why_it_helps: The claim page had a hidden counter meant to tell us whether people who don't sign up are (a) never touching the email box or (b) touching it and giving up -- the answer decides what to fix next. The counter was missing people whose phones auto-fill the email, and losing anyone browsing privately. This fixes both so the reading we take in early August is trustworthy.
changes_in_plain_words: The claim page now counts someone as 'touched the email box' even when their phone auto-fills or they paste the address, not only when they tap the box first -- so the count stops being smaller than the number who actually signed up.
It counts each person only once no matter how they touch the box.
People using a private or in-app browser (where the phone blocks our usual memory) now still get grouped correctly as one person instead of being dropped from the tally.
A small reporting-tool bug that mislabeled this counter as 'unknown' is fixed so our reports read cleanly.
change.why_the_rate_is_what_it_is: This ships against a MEASUREMENT step, not an exchange step, so there is no user 'price' being paid -- the change alters nothing the visitor sees, gives, or gets. It exists so the email-gate exchange (the discount+video is the price of the email) can be diagnosed honestly before anyone tries to reprice it.
what_would_have_to_be_true: 'input' reliably fires on autofill and paste in the mobile browsers/in-app webviews QR traffic uses (it does per the DOM spec and is the standard autofill-detection hook; exercised in verification).

All three claim events (page_viewed, email_field_engaged, email_entered) fire within a single page load, so an in-memory fallback id links them (true -- the claim page is a single-page flow with no reload between them).
The once-guard prevents double counting when both 'focus' and 'input' fire on the same visit (a shared boolean flag; verified to hold across focus+input+input).
change.second_order_effects: email_field_engaged counts will rise once autofill/paste sessions are captured, and visitor_id-null rows will drop -- so post-fix numbers are NOT comparable to any pre-fix baseline for this event; the changelog and ANALYTICS.md state the discontinuity and treat pre-fix rows as lower bounds. No conversion event changes: email_entered, video_started, review_clicked and their cross-app linking (which key on email/operation_id, not visitor_id) are untouched, so no verdict funnel is disturbed. The in-memory id is per page load so it never over-links across visits. One step further: making the biggest-leak diagnostic trustworthy is what enables next cycle to choose a MECHANISM fix (the kind history says moves this funnel) instead of a presentation reshuffle (the kind that went flat).
change.strongest_case_against: A sharp sceptic says: this is the THIRD consecutive measurement-only cycle (07-16, 07-20, now) on a project whose owner keeps listing CONVERSION as the target -- you are polishing instruments while the funnel sits still, and 4-vs-6 over two days is too thin to justify touching anything. Honest answer: the defect is a code certainty, not a statistical claim -- a focus-only listener demonstrably cannot see an autofill and a null id demonstrably cannot be linked -- and the cost of NOT fixing it is concrete and time-boxed: the early-August read (the entire payoff of last cycle) would be corrupted and we would lose another month. Every conversion alternative this cycle requires betting on a cause I cannot verify (PostHog 403; no in-app replays), the exact unverified-cause mistake the last cycle was faulted for. Given a two-week clock to the read, repairing the instrument now is the highest-integrity, highest-EV move; and I am explicitly committing the next cycle to a mechanism-level conversion bet driven by the repaired read.

tradeoff.gained: A trustworthy first read (~early August) of WHERE the biggest, most review-critical leak actually leaks -- never-engaged vs engaged-and-declined -- the prerequisite to any real fix and thus to more videos and more reviews.
tradeoff.risked: Opportunity cost of a cycle spent on measurement rather than a conversion experiment. Quantified downside to live conversion is ~0 (no user-facing change; conversion logging and cross-app linking untouched). The only numeric risk is analytic: email_field_engaged counts are discontinuous across the fix, so pre-fix rows must be treated as lower bounds -- flagged in the changelog and ANALYTICS.md. Downstream review-reminder path is unaffected: this change touches neither email capture nor Klaviyo.
unverified_assumptions: OWNER QUESTION / FACT CORRECTION to raise, not resolve: FUNNEL_CONTEXT states as [FACT] that the QR link carries ONLY ?sku (no code, no source). But session-recording start_urls show ~83% of claim traffic now arriving with code=GOTYOU30 and source=insert|box, and claim.html reads params.get('code') into state.discountCode and passes it to Klaviyo as discount_code. Is GOTYOU30 a real, redeemable, MULTI-USE 30% code now printed on the insert cards? If yes, a documented premise of the email gate is weaker than recorded. Showing a code up front remains owner-rejected, so this is a FACT to correct and a strategic question -- NOT a lever this change pulls.
Whether the instrument miss is mostly autofill vs blocked-storage (N=6 cannot size it); the fix is correct for either and harmless if neither applies to a given session.

OWNER QUESTION (carried from 2026-07-20, still blocking): can the PostHog personal API key be regranted the query:read scope? Without it the whole claim top-of-funnel is measurable only once the durable events accumulate -- the single biggest measurement blocker.

change.differs_from_past_attempt: NOT PR #8 (a claim-page layout/hierarchy REDESIGN for capture -> flat; this ships ZERO presentation/UI change). NOT the owner-rejected code-first move (this shows and gives away nothing; the email exchange is untouched). NOT the owner-rejected review-link-in-video-email (this touches no email surface). It REPAIRS two defects in the 2026-07-20 instrument (focus-only listener; null visitor_id) that its own 'verified live' synthetic test could not surface because synthetic POSTs neither autofill nor run in a storage-blocked webview. It also does not repeat the last cycle's error of aiming a fix at an unverified early-exit cause; here the cause is a code certainty and the change is measurement-only.
change.verification: node --check tools/funnel-report.mjs -> OK; parsed both inline <script> blocks in claim.html -> 0 errors. Booted the app (PORT=3939 node --experimental-websocket server.js) and fetched claim.html?sku=PTT-GREEN1&code=GOTYOU30&source=insert -> HTTP 200, with focus+input listeners, the shared once-guard, and the in-memory visitor_id fallback all present in the response and the old {once:true} block removed. Drove the ACTUAL edited code (extracted getVisitorId + wireEmailFieldEngaged) under a mocked DOM: (A) input-only, no focus (autofill/paste) fired exactly ONE email_field_engaged; (B) focus+type+type fired exactly ONE (once-guard held), visitor_id stable and non-null; (C) storage blocked -> all claim events shared ONE non-null in-memory visitor_id (PASS). Ran funnel-report 14 --until=2026-07-22 -> email_field_engaged now printed in canonical order (email_field_engaged 4 right after page_viewed 49, before email_entered 103), no '(non-canonical!)' flag. No Supabase test rows were created (the behavioral test mocked the network), so none to delete.

pr_body:
## What this does

This is a **behind-the-scenes measurement fix on the claim page** (the QR landing screen). A visitor sees nothing different -- there is no design or copy change. It repairs a hidden counter we added on 2026-07-20 so the reading we take from it in early August is trustworthy.

## Verdict on the last change (2026-07-06 -- remove the message-step friction)

Still **not yet measurable**, and it stays pending. The exact headline metric it was graded on (arrived in app -> started a video, from PostHog) could not be reproduced this cycle because the PostHog query API is locked out (403, missing scope). On the nearest durable stand-in (picked a role -> started a video, matched per person): before 59.0% (23 of 39) -> after 60.9% (28 of 46), +1.9 points, p=0.86 -- **statistically indistinguishable from noise**, so it may not be called a win or a loss. A separate encouraging read (gave email -> started video) went 35.3% (24 of 68) -> 45.9% (28 of 61), +10.6 points, but p=0.22 -- **also not statistically solid**, so treat the direction as suggestive only, not proven.

## The leaks, ranked by value to reviews

1. **The claim-page email box** -- ~66% of people who scan never type a single key (43 of 65 sampled screen replays this window; ~57% prior). Biggest drop by headcount and it gates everything: no email means no code, no video, and no in-app review ask (all 11 review clicks this window came from the in-app thank-you screen). Caveat: replay sampling is capped at 100/window, so this is directional, not exact.
2. **Gave email -> started the free video** -- ~54% of already-warm users never start it (45.9%, 28 of 61; not a proven change vs 35.3% prior, p=0.22). High value, but we can't yet tell WHICH sub-step loses them, so a fix would be a guess.
3. **The review ask on the preview/share screens** -- ~0 clicks despite real traffic. Lowest value: it's a second, worse-placed ask after the in-app thank-you already collected the review intent.

## What the QA auditor said, and how I responded

The independent auditor **approved** the plan, with three minor (non-blocking) notes:
- *This is the third measurement-only cycle in a row, on a project whose owner names conversion as the goal.* Fair, and acknowledged. The repair is genuinely time-boxed -- it has to land before the early-August reading accumulates or we lose a month -- and every conversion experiment available this cycle would rest on a cause we cannot verify right now (PostHog locked out, no in-app replays), which is exactly the mistake that sank the last cycle. I've committed the **next** cycle to a real conversion change driven by the repaired reading; a fourth measurement-only cycle would not be defensible.
- *A documented 'fact' in our notes is now wrong: claim traffic is arriving with a code (GOTYOU30) and a source tag, not the 'just a product code' the notes claim.* I raised this to you as a question and a correction, and built nothing on it. **Question for you:** is GOTYOU30 a real, reusable 30% code now printed on the insert cards? If so, one assumption behind the email gate is weaker than we recorded.
- *The fix relies on the browser 'input' signal firing on auto-fill; correct per spec but browser-dependent.* I addressed this by actually driving the code: I confirmed an auto-fill/paste with no tap now counts exactly once, and a private/in-app-browser session stays grouped as one person.

## What this change does and why

The claim page has a hidden counter meant to tell us whether people who don't sign up (a) never touch the email box, or (b) touch it and give up -- and those two answers need completely different fixes. Two bugs were making that counter lie:
- It only counted people who **tapped** the box first, so anyone whose phone **auto-fills or pastes** their email (common on mobile) was signing up without ever being counted -- the counter was reading *lower* than the number who actually submitted, which is impossible for a true count.
- People on **private or in-app browsers** (a big share of QR traffic) were being dropped from the per-person tally entirely.

Both are now fixed: the box counts auto-fill and paste (once per person), and private-browser sessions stay linkable. A small reporting-tool label bug was fixed too. **No conversion logic, email capture, or video delivery is touched.**

## How I verified it

- Checked the code parses cleanly and booted the app locally; the claim page returns HTTP 200 with all three fixes present.
- Drove the actual edited code: an auto-fill/paste with no tap counts exactly once; tap-then-type still counts exactly once; a storage-blocked session keeps one shared person-id across all its events.
- Ran the report and confirmed the counter now appears correctly labeled (no 'unknown' flag).

## What to re-measure, and roughly when

Around **early August** (~2026-08-05, after ~2 weeks of clean post-fix data), run the two per-person step-to-step measurements: landed -> touched the email box, and touched the box -> submitted an email, and significance-test each. Because the counter's numbers jump after this fix, **pre-2026-07-22 counts are a lower bound and can't be compared to post-fix counts** -- both windows must sit on/after 07-22. That reading is what lets the next cycle aim a real conversion fix at a verified cause instead of a guess.
telegram_summary: Last change (07-06, message-step fix): still NOT provable -- role->video 59%->61% p=0.86, and gave-email->video 35%->46% p=0.22, both inside the noise. PostHog stayed locked out this cycle. Top leak: the claim page's email box -- ~66% of scanners never type a key; it gates every video and review. This cycle I fixed a behind-the-scenes counter on that page so it correctly counts people whose phones auto-fill/paste their email and people on private browsers -- nothing a visitor sees changes. It makes our early-August reading of WHY people skip the email trustworthy, so next cycle can aim a real fix. Auditor approved. Q for you: is GOTYOU30 a real reusable code now printed on the cards?
